4 · Physical architecture & design 4d
YQYorik
Failures are expected, and handled
If…
A message arrives twice
Ignored: its (event ID, consumer) is already recorded
If…
A message keeps failing
Moved to a dead-letter queue after 5 tries; an alarm fires
If…
Publishing fails
The event stays in the outbox and is retried
No lost events
No double notifications
Bad messages isolated

WZEric
Logical decisions (AD-02 to AD-06)
IDDecisionWhy
AD-02Split where no transaction crosses, not by nounsPayment and expiry stay one transaction, so no sagas. Five services rejected (50–55 person-days)
AD-03One database and one database role per serviceNo joins across services; enforced by grants and architecture tests
AD-04Outbox → SNS → SQS with dead-letter queues; consumers skip duplicatesEvents are never lost or applied twice, and there is no broker to run
AD-05One shared login session in Valkey, roles inside itServices check roles without calling identity on every request
AD-06One direct call, commerce → identity, failing closedAn outage returns an error and Stripe retries; a buyer is never wrongly rejected

Physical decisions (AD-07 to AD-14)
IDDecisionWhy
AD-07Fargate on ARM, not Kubernetes (EKS)The EKS control plane (≈ US$73/month) costs more than all our compute; ARM is ~20% cheaper
AD-08Fargate Spot above the minimum (1 : 3)Cheap extra capacity; the minimum stays on regular Fargate
AD-09CloudFront → load balancer with a secret headerHTTPS at the edge; the load balancer refuses everything else (403)
AD-10Small NAT instance, not a NAT Gateway≈ US$4 instead of ≈ US$43 a month
AD-11One database server, three databasesLow cost; moving a database to its own server needs no code change
AD-12Permanent edge, disposable runtime≈ US$0.12–0.20 an hour while up, instead of ≈ US$125 a month always on
AD-13No Kubernetes or Argo CDThey would cost 8–12 days of set-up before any feature work
AD-14Own account in an AWS OrganizationSeparate blast radius and bill; short-lived logins; guardrails the account admin cannot lift

WZEric
Context map: where service boundaries may go
  • Identity → Google: anti-corruption layer (the OAuth gateway port)
  • Identity → commerce: customer and supplier, one synchronous call (the user port)
  • Commerce → Stripe: anti-corruption layer (checkout and refund gateways, webhook)
  • Commerce → notification: published language: version 1 events over SNS → SQS
Four contexts share one service because they share transactions; the map shows where network boundaries are allowed to be.
BlocBuy Team 8 · SWE5001
Backup · not presented unless asked
B3
Backup · Q&A only B4
WZEric
Aggregates and their life cycles
  • Team (GroupDeal): only OPEN may change state, and only once
  • Order: PENDING → CONFIRMED or CANCELLED
  • Purchase intent is the order-side aggregate
  • Also: checkout payment, refund work, product with team terms, notification
  • Domain events: MemberJoined, TeamSucceeded, TeamExpired, PaymentSucceeded
  • In the same transaction, the outbox writer turns them into versioned integration events
Be ready to explain: FAILED and CANCELED are allowed by the status table, but nothing in the code triggers them yet.

Everything the real cloud taught us
What happenedWhat we did
The first promotion failed five times (image digests, variables, a tag policy, an early 503)Fixed one at a time; first green run on 6 Oct
A read-only container disk crashed the web server's temp folderMounted a writable /tmp
The AWS tagging API still lists resources that are already deletedThe teardown check asks each service directly
Default database privileges exposed tables to every roleGrants set after each migration, and tested
The outbox relay marked unsent rows as failed after a mid-batch errorCaught in code review and fixed
The notification consumer was never switched on in AWSNow enabled together with messaging
Setting up scaling was denied: tags need an extra permissionPermission added, limited to this project (17 Oct)
The deploy stopped twice: alarm e-mails were not yet confirmedTesting opt-out for now; confirm the e-mails before the final release
An interrupted start-up leaves auto-scaling pausedRepaired by hand; no fix yet
An organisation policy blocked CloudFront metrics (us-east-1)Policies consolidated with a narrow exception

StackLifetimeContents
